quests.title: Through the Gates of Ivory

dialogue.t: Oh! Looks like it's time! Everyone's heading toward the assembly hall.
We'd better catch up!
{NICKNAME}, you're already worn out? But what about the fun activities afterward...

dialogue.sit: You're right. Let's go see what fun activities they've saved for after the main event.
That can wait. First, let's see the main course.

dialogue.t: —Yay! —Mhm!

dialogue.sit: Exhaustion seems to have finally caught up with you. You and Paimon curl up together on the sofa, drifting into a light doze. Then, somewhere between sleep and waking, ten faint chimes ring out...

dialogue.section: Eye of Graeae, Intoxicated Snegovik, Pavlina, Hesitant Snegovik, Rational Snegovik, Ikhor, Aksinya

dialogue.t: Paimon's starting to feel a little nervous. It's like the Chicken-Mushroom Skewer she had this morning is dancing around in her stomach... Ugh.
Paimon wonders what Pavlina, the princess of the Snegurochka, is like... and what kind of person the groom is, too...
If Aglaya's story is anything to go by, Pavlina sounds completely enchanted with him. Humans even tried to steal him away! He must be some once-in-a-lifetime heartthrob.
...Maybe this wedding is more than it seems.
If what {NICKNAME} saw in the Pale Crown Palace really happened, then Pavlina was one of the people who betrayed Miss Aksinya... Which means...
Pavlina probably has one of the pieces of your body.
Right. The one who has the fragmented power of my body is... Ikhor. So I suspect the groom may be...
Pavlina! Pavlina!
Whoa! Where did she come from?
She's the mistress of this place. A trick like that is child's play for her.
But... no. How did she...?

dialogue.sit: What have you found out?

dialogue.t: Just as I expected. She carries a piece of my body's power in her life too.
Huh?
Today is a special day. We were a people that no one ever blessed or cared for. But that changes now.
Love is what truly feeds the soul.
We were born without souls, so we chased after love because we longed to have one. We live for love, and we live because of love.
Yes. Human love is what gives us souls. It is what allows us to become beings in our own right.
But the humans who share their souls with us, they can be such terrible creditors who end up forcing us to live by the rules of their fickle love...
Larisa once stood here, too. You all saw the betrayal with your own eyes — treachery so vile, it cost her both her soul and her life.
But her death brought no shame upon us. On the contrary, it was something to be proud of, for it proved that nobility was always part of her nature.
Nevertheless, her passing was a great loss to us, for there was no Snegurochka more pure-minded than Larisa.
Pavlina, though... During her time at Hvergelmir — no, perhaps even before then... she had already been tainted by human ways.
That would probably explain why she sees things this way. It is the sort of idea only a human could have, even if Pavlina herself does not realize it.

dialogue.sit: Looks like not everyone agrees with her.

dialogue.t: Actually, what Paimon really wants to know is, is that going to be your speech at the wedding? It sure doesn't sound like one...
...Her wrongful death will be the final page in our kind's tragic chapter.
The new beginning granted to us by the gods shall soon arrive, and from this day forward, our soulless past shall finally come to an end.
You never knew the truth, and there is no need for you to know it now... For this day to come, a sacrifice had already been made some time ago.
Huh? What's happening??? It feels like the air in the room has just changed all of a sudden...
Come to us, soul-water, born of the gods and made for the gods.
Come to us, Ikhor. Come. Offer yourself up for our sake.
...Wait, he's the groom? Hey! Ikhor!
He can't seem to hear Paimon... What's wrong with him? Did someone do this to him? Or is it that shackle?
We have to do something, {NICKNAME}! Paimon has a feeling this "ritual" isn't the wedding we thought it was going to be...
No, it isn't. It is a ritual to transfer the power held in my body...
However the Snegurochka princess came to possess that fragment of power before, she must have found a way to claim the rest of it now...
She wants to defy the natural order and give those under her protection souls. But she would never be able to do that by herself alone. And that is where that power comes in.
Then we must do something now! She's going to take him!
Say it, Ikhor. Do you promise to give us what we've been wishing for?
Yes, I do.
I object to this ritual! ...I know this is probably the last thing anyone wants to hear right now, but a Court Jester is supposed to speak up when advice is needed, isn't she?
...Aksinya. Though I do not know how you managed to escape that inescapable prison... But you were not invited to today's proceedings.
Yes, yes, you already told me that earlier today. With not a trace of kindness left for an old colleague. How sad.
But you and I both know I have every right to be here — as an uninvited guest.
Stop it!
Why keep on fighting when you know it won't change anything? You know you won't win, not even now.
I know. And that's why I came with some help this time.
A cheap little trick. All that will do is buy you a little time...

dialogue.sit:
You simply do not understand, Aksinya. The sacrifice has already been made. That means the ending has already been set in motion, and there is nothing you can do to stop it.
So I failed this time. But what difference does it make? It's just one more "rehearsal"...
Next time... Next time, it will work...

dialogue.t: ...{NICKNAME}... {NICKNAME}!
Whew — there you are! Did the bell wake you? You were completely out. Is the bed here really that comfy?

dialogue.sit: I think I had a dream.

dialogue.t: No wonder. You were asleep for a long time. Paimon's been keeping watch the whole while. Was it a nice dream, or a scary one?
Actually, never mind. Tell Paimon later. Now's not really the time.
Do you remember what happened earlier? We came to the House of Hesperides for a wedding.

dialogue.sit: But that "ritual" wasn't a wedding at all.

dialogue.t: That towering princess of the Snegurochka, Pavlina... She nearly killed Ikhor...
Paimon knows Ikhor isn't really human, strictly speaking. He's just a fragment of the power that originally belonged to Goggles. But even so...
Compassion is something to be respected, Miss Paimon.
Thanks, Goggles. Oh, right, when Pavlina cast her spell, Goggles was the one who protected us and brought us here, somewhere safe.
While you were asleep, Paimon did some poking around. Looks like someone named Myshkin used to live here. Didn't Aglaya mention him when she first welcomed us?
...*cough* Hello? Do you copy? You should be able to hear what I'm saying?

*sigh* Thanks for nothing, you two. I poured so much effort into getting "him" out, even if in part... Only for you to send him right back, as if nothing had happened. Pavlina almost won right there and then.
Huh? Aksinya! Wait, how are you coming through Goggl—?
Ha! I am the creator of the Eye of Graeae, after all. I can still make use of some of its functions.
...Hmm. It's been a while since we last met, eh, dear colleague? Don't you think you're getting "a bit too passionate" right now?
Ah, sorry, that wasn't meant for you. I'm currently busy dealing with that crazy shrew... How tragic, Pavlina of the Snegovik. You've completely lost it.
Her gaze is like Prime Ice, but her mind is like a powderkeg. A single spark could set her off and destroy all around her.
I've trapped Pavlina, but have little time for anything else right now. Take "his" fragments away from here, one by one, while her grip on this area is weakened, away from her grasp.
That's the only way to ensure that shrew won't be able to offer up "his" power for her people.
We have to take back all that power, don't we? It's not the same as why she seeks your power, is it? "To have a body once more"... that's what you wish for, isn't it?
Y—Yes...
Then go. I won't be able to hold out for long... Hurry—
She's gone...
Take Goggles' fragments... one by one? What does she even mean? Doesn't she know that Pavlina has some of Goggles' power too???

dialogue.sit: She may have something else up her sleeves too.

dialogue.t: Yeah... Better take what she says with a huge rock of salt. But what should we do now then?
Hey, you know what? This is about Goggles! We should ask what he wants.
I think... Maybe we should gather at least some of the power that has been split up, and try to make him as complete as possible. Then we can take it all back.
This may sound a little ironic, but my wish is for the fragments, incomplete as they are, to be as whole as possible...
It's just like how the Snegurochka princess must have decided to perform the ritual because she wanted to help her people become more "whole."
And that is something I can understand, and even empathize with, to some degree.
How can you feel for her!? She was gonna gobble you up, piece by piece, just to get what she wanted!!!
Paimon can share her food or Mora with other folks, no problem. But if you want Paimon to hand over an arm or a leg...
Or even Paimon's hair! Hmm... Actually, hair seems alright... especially if it's just a few strands—— Anyway, that's not the point.
It doesn't matter what the other person's reasons are. This is something... something Paimon needs to think over! Very carefully! Though Paimon probably won't say yes anyway, to be honest...

dialogue.sit: Yes. It's not good to over-deplete yourself for the sake of others.

dialogue.t: ...You are right. But that aside, there is another reason we must reclaim him "whole."
Another reason? And what would that be?

dialogue.sit: That you don't need to know, Paimon.

dialogue.t: Huh? Are the two of you keeping something from Paimon!? And Paimon's not talking about secret snack stashes or anything like tha——

dialogue.sit: We should get moving.

dialogue.t: I have marked the fragment locations. Let's go, before the clock strikes ten.
Hmm. It feels like the farther up the mountain we go, the heavier the storm gets...
Huh? What's this?
It's an invitation...
An invitation? Let Paimon take a look... Hmm. It says Pavlina, Grand Duchess of the Snegurochka, is inviting... whoever's holding this invitation to attend a wedding...?
"Those who wish to attend the ceremony may present this invitation as proof that they have been invited..."
Hmm... So the wedding is being held at... House of Hesp-something, up on the snowy mountain...
House of Hesperides. Yes. It was once home to the sovereign who ruled over the Snegovik. As for Pavlina...
That name does sound faintly familiar...
So, Pavlina, the princess of the Snegurochka, might be tied to Goggles' past too?
Most likely.
The house's all the way up the mountain? And we still have to climb higher?
I'm afraid so. Unless House of Hesperides somehow moved in the last five hundred years...
Fine. Then let's keep going and check it out.
（静静地躺在地上，仿佛从未有过生命。）$UNRELEASED
Huh, this lamp is weird. But for some reason... now that we're near it, the blizzard's easing up. It even feels kind of warm...
Wait a minute. Paimon's heard that if you suddenly start feeling warm on a snowy mountain, it could mean you're so cold you're starting to hallucinate...

dialogue.sit: Then I guess I'm hallucinating too!
Then we should probably keep telling ourselves we're freezing...

dialogue.t: Aha! So you felt it too! It really is getting warmer!
Don't worry, you two. This is a special lamp. They say it was blessed by the fae that is now inside it a long time ago.
It offers some protection from the cold.
Whoa! D—did someone just... appear out of nowhere?
Hello, my flying friend.
This is my lamp. I left it here earlier when I got a little bored and went for a walk.
Oh, so it's yours... Wait, you went for a walk in this blizzard? Dressed like that? How are you not freezing?
...Freezing?
Should I be reacting to temperature changes? Is that what you were expecting?
Uh... That's not really the point. Most people would freeze solid if they wore that little in this weather like this.

dialogue.sit: Maybe all the shivering is what keeps them from freezing...
I suppose there are some peoples who do fine in the cold?

dialogue.t: Right, because all that shivering would totally warm them up... As if! But that's only for regular people.
The fae don't really mind the cold. Just look at the Snegovik and the Jack Frosts. They probably don't do well in a place that's too warm.
But you don't look like a fae, and you're not cold either... So who are you, anyway? And what are you doing out here with no luggage and barely any warm clothes on?
I... I am Ikhor. Someone... a woman told me to leave the house, but she didn't tell me where to go. So I've just been waiting here.
The house...? You mean the House of Hesperides? We're on our way there for some wedding.
Paimon's never been to a Snegovik wedding before. They say the Snegovik live for love, right? So their weddings must be super romantic!
A wedding... Yes. For the Snegovik, it is an important <color=#00E1FFFF>ritual.</color> They have been preparing for it for a long time.
So it must be a really big deal, right? Hehe, how exciting! Oh, right. Who's the woman you were talking about? You know, the one who told you to leave the house.
I have no idea. I'd never met her before that.
H—hold on! You mean to say that someone you didn't even know told you to leave the house, and you just went along with it!?
Yes. Because that was what she wanted, and she wanted it very badly. And if someone wanted something so badly that it becomes a wish, of course I should grant it.
({NICKNAME}... He doesn't look that young, but the way he talks and acts is just like a little child. He feels a little... not all there...)
...I can sense it. There's definitely a part of my body's power that's inside him.
(Wait, really? We found it already?)
But the power inside him is incomplete. That may be why his mind seems a little... not quite there as well. The power that's in him... is so broken up that it's impossible to recover.
Huh? Then what do we do now?
Before I can reclaim this part of my power, it must be restored to a more complete state first... I sense that the part of my body here was split up through a special ritual of some kind.
If only I could get closer to the core of that power. Then I might be able to give you a clearer answer.

dialogue.sit: (Sounds like we should head over to the wedding then.)

dialogue.t: (So are we taking him with us? Hmm... We can't just leave him here. But we still don't know why that person made him leave the house...)
Um... This is kind of a strange favor to ask, but could you show us the way to the House of Hesperides?
We... don't really know the area, you see, and you're from there, so... you'd be the perfect guide!
Is this your wish?

dialogue.sit: Yes. Could you help me out with it?

dialogue.t: And Paimon thinks it'd be better for you, too! Even if you don't get cold, it just doesn't feel right for us to leave you out here in this storm dressed like that.
"People do not always know what is best for them. They choose storms in the morning, then pray for peace by night."
Hmm?
Someone once told me that. While I do not feel the cold, maybe you are right.
So long as someone asks it of me, I am willing to grant their wish. Now, allow me to fulfill yours. Please follow me.

A house...? You mean there's a house up here on this snowy mountain? With people living in it?
Yes, there is a house. It is called the House of Hesperides, and it is where the Snegovik live. The lady of the house is Pavlina, the Snegurochka princess.
Right now... I believe she is preparing for her wedding.
A Snegovik wedding?
Paimon's never been to a Snegovik wedding before. They say the Snegovik live for love, right? So their weddings must be super romantic!
A wedding... Yes. For the Snegovik, it is an important <color=#00E1FFFF>ritual.</color> They have been preparing for it for a long time.
So it must be a really big deal, right? Hehe, how exciting! Hmm... Do you think we can go see it?
Is that what you wish for?
Well, with the storm this bad, it'd be nice to have somewhere to rest for a bit... And besides, we'd get to see a Snegovik wedding...

dialogue.sit: So this is Paimon's wish, then?
Then it's my wish too.

dialogue.t: Yeah, yeah!
I understand. In that case, please take this...
Oh, what's that?
This is a wedding invitation. With it, the house will receive you... as honored guests of the ritual.
But um... isn't this invite yours?
No... friend who is named Paimon. Invitations are only for guests.
Oh, okay! Thank you then! Oh, right... Who's the woman you were talking about? You know, the one who told you to leave the house.
I have no idea. I'd never met her before that.
H—hold on! You mean to say that someone you didn't even know told you to leave the house, and you just went along with it!?
Yes. Because that was what she wanted, and she wanted it very badly. And if someone wanted something so badly that it becomes a wish, of course I should grant it.

Someone once told me that. While I do not feel the cold, maybe you are right.
So long as someone asks it of me, I am willing to grant their wish. Now, allow me to fulfill yours. Please follow me.
Myshkin? Is that you? You're finally here...
...Huh? Who's Myshkin? No, we're just passing adventurers — {NICKNAME} and Paimon!
We heard there was a wedding happening here, so we came by to take a look! And we do have an invite, so it's not like we're crashing the wedding, right?
Please present your invitation to the statue by the door.
The statue? Uh... okay, sure...
(Ikhor, you came from in there, right? Then you must know this place better than we do. Do they always have weird rules like this?)
(This does not seem to be part of the "ritual.")
(So you're just as lost as we are. Well, since we're already here, let's just do what she said for now.)
Welcome to the House of Hesperides.
Since you have an invitation, then you are guests of this house, and every guest deserves a proper welcome. You may call me Aglaya.
Is this your first time attending a Snegovik wedding?

dialogue.sit: Mmhmm.

dialogue.t: You two do not seem to be from around here, so I take it you have not heard about the scandal. I doubt you would have been willing to come here if you had.
A scandal?
At least, humans would call it that. The last ceremonial ritual we held on this scale was Larisa's wedding.
But that human betrayed her in the end. She killed him, and then the vow took her life, too.
Larisa was the most beautiful of us all... even the way she died was beautiful.
That day, her fury brought down a blizzard so fierce, it froze even the bolts of lightning mid-fall. You should have seen that beautiful, deadly Prime Ice magic...
Umm...
Heh, but you have no cause for worry. You will be safe here at the House of Hesperides, as long as you stay away from what is forbidden.
The ritual will begin when <color=#00E1FFFF>the clock strikes eight times</color>. Please make your way to the chapel right away when you hear it.
Until then, you may look around the main hall... The other rooms are not open to guests...
But you are welcome to enjoy the entertainment here, or simply rest for a while. The choice is yours.

dialogue.sit: So, about those rooms we're not allowed into...

dialogue.t: Some of those are private quarters. We even have one set aside for the bride and groom...

dialogue.sit: Ah, excuse. I didn't mean to be rude.

dialogue.t: Once, there was a human woman who dared sneak into the groom's room while he was alone. Of course, she was caught almost immediately...
Wh-what!? Was she trying to steal the groom or something???
Not from Pavlina, the Snegurochka princess. What Pavlina has laid claim to, no one takes from her.
So cold is she by nature, she hardly seems like a Snegurochka at all. But that boy was hers, and there was no way she would let anyone take him away.
...Regardless of that, the ritual will go ahead, and we will succeed this time. She has sworn it on the sword Larisa once wielded.
And we all know what happens to those who break their vows.
Enough of the dull introductions. This ritual is one that is worth celebrating after all. I wish the both of you a most pleasant and unforgettable day here at the House of Hesperides.
Oh my, you ended up all the way over here?
Let's get you back where you're supposed to be.
Huh? Where did Ikhor go? Goggles, did you see where he went?
My apologies. Some special ritual power seems to be affecting this entire place. I can no longer sense his presence. Given some time, I may be able to determine what's going on...
Honestly, Paimon still had so many questions for him. Like, if he's obviously just one part of one part of Goggles' body, how does he have a whole body of his own...?
That part is easy enough to understand. It is like... "A pomegranate split open, its seeds scattered across the ground. Piece the shell back together, and it can still, just barely, be called whole."
Ugh... Okay, even if he isn't really human, that example was still pretty creepy.
But we're out of leads for now, so we'll just have to wait for Goggles to figure things out.
Come on, {NICKNAME}, let's go soak up the wedding atmosphere! It's not every day you get to see a Snegovik wedding!
Huh? Where did Ikhor go? Goggles, did you see where he went?
My apologies. Some special ritual power seems to be affecting this entire place. I can no longer sense his presence. Given some time, I may be able to determine what's going on...
Honestly, Paimon still had so many questions for him. Like, if he's obviously just one part of one part of Goggles' body, how does he have a whole body of his own...?
That part is easy enough to understand. It is like... "A pomegranate split open, its seeds scattered across the ground. Piece the shell back together, and it can still, just barely, be called whole."
Ugh... Okay, even if he isn't really human, that example was still pretty creepy.
But we're out of leads for now, so we'll just have to wait for Goggles to figure things out.
Come on, {NICKNAME}, let's go soak up the wedding atmosphere!
...As far as I know, Pavlina, princess of the Snegurochka, isn't really the type to marry a human. How strange.
If anything... I would have thought she'd be more attached to her own kind than to humans...
Well, you never know! Maybe she met the one and went, "Hehe, I don't care what anyone says! I'm marrying him!"
It's possible, but the chances are slim.
Still... perhaps the wedding itself is the clue.
Okay, then let's go to the wedding and see what we can find out! It's a Snegovik wedding, after all!
The wedding is about to begin. We ask our guests to wait in the hall in the meantime...
The wedding is about to begin. We ask our guests to wait in the hall in the meantime...
{NICKNAME}, you're already worn out? But what about the fun activities afterward...

dialogue.sit: That can wait. First, let's see the main course.
You're right. Let's go see what fun activities they've saved for after the main event.

dialogue.t: All right, Paimon's with you.

dialogue.sit: Exhaustion seems to have finally caught up with you. You and Paimon curl up together on the sofa, drifting into a light doze. Then, somewhere between sleep and waking, eight faint chimes ring out...

dialogue.t: Should we wait here until the wedding starts?

dialogue.sit: Alright, let's do that.
Hold on. There are still a few things we need to do.
Exhaustion seems to have finally caught up with you. You and Paimon curl up together on the sofa, drifting into a light doze. Then, somewhere between sleep and waking, eight faint chimes ring out...

dialogue.t: The "ritual" is already underway. Please go on in... There's no need to be anywhere else...
(test)客人你好，请不要靠近礼台$UNRELEASED
The "ritual" is already underway. Please go on in... There's no need to be anywhere else...
The "ritual" is already underway. Please go on in... There's no need to be anywhere else...
Paimon's starting to feel a little nervous. It's like the Chicken-Mushroom Skewer she had this morning is dancing around in her stomach... Ugh.
Paimon wonders what Pavlina, the princess of the Snegurochka, is like... and what kind of person the groom is, too...
If Aglaya's story is anything to go by, Pavlina sounds completely enchanted with him. Humans even tried to steal him away! He must be some once-in-a-lifetime heartthrob.
Oh! And then there's Ikhor. He doesn't seem to be here either. Come to think of it, what was he doing in this mansion in the first place...?

dialogue.sit: The princess of the Snegurochka has to be connected to all this somehow.

dialogue.t: Paimon was thinking the same thing. But today's supposed to be a happy occasion, and everyone's here to offer her their blessings.
If we catch her in a good mood, maybe she'll let a clue or two slip.
I have my doubts, Miss Paimon. Still, I agree. This is a good chance to gather clues up close.
Pavlina! Pavlina!
Whoa! Where did she come from?
She's the mistress of this place. A trick like that is child's play for her.
But... no. How did she...?

dialogue.sit: What have you found out?

dialogue.t: I sense that she carries a piece of my body's power in her life too. How is that even possible?
Huh?
Today is a special day. We were a people that no one ever blessed or cared for. But that changes now.
Love is what truly feeds the soul.
We were born without souls, so we chased after love because we longed to have one. We live for love, and we live because of love.
Yes. Human love is what gives us souls. It is what allows us to become beings in our own right.
But the humans who share their souls with us, they can be such terrible creditors who end up forcing us to live by the rules of their fickle love...
Larisa once stood here, too. You all saw the betrayal with your own eyes — treachery so vile, it cost her both her soul and her life.
But her death brought no shame upon us. On the contrary, it was something to be proud of, for it proved that nobility was always part of her nature.
Nevertheless, her passing was a great loss to us, for there was no Snegurochka more pure-minded than Larisa.
Pavlina, though... During her time at Hvergelmir — no, perhaps even before then... she had already been tainted by human ways.
That would probably explain why she sees things this way. It is the sort of idea only a human could have, even if Pavlina herself does not realize it.

dialogue.sit: Looks like not everyone agrees with her.

dialogue.t: Actually, what Paimon really wants to know is, is that going to be your speech at the wedding? It sure doesn't sound like one...
...Her wrongful death will be the final page in our kind's tragic chapter.
The new beginning granted to us by the gods shall soon arrive, and from this day forward, our soulless past shall finally come to an end.
You never knew the truth, and there is no need for you to know it now... For this day to come, a sacrifice had already been made some time ago.
Huh? What's happening??? It feels like the air in the room has just changed all of a sudden...
Come to us, soul-water, born of the gods and made for the gods.
Come to us, Ikhor. Come. Offer yourself up for our sake.
...Wait, he's the groom? Hey! Ikhor!
He can't seem to hear Paimon... What's wrong with him? Did someone do this to him? Or is it that shackle?
We have to do something, {NICKNAME}! Paimon has a feeling this "ritual" isn't the wedding we thought it was going to be...
I'm afraid you're right.
However the Snegurochka princess came to possess that fragment of power before, she must have found a way to claim the rest of it now...
She wants to defy the natural order and give those under her protection souls. But she would never be able to do that by herself alone. And that is where that power comes in.
Then we must do something now! She's going to take him!
Say it, Ikhor. Do you promise to give us what we've been wishing for?
Yes, I do.
I object to this union!
...I know this is probably the last thing anyone wants to hear right now, but a Court Jester is supposed to speak up when advice is needed, isn't she?
...Aksinya. Though I do not know how you managed to escape that inescapable prison... But you were not invited to today's proceedings.
Yes, yes, you already told me that earlier today. With not a trace of kindness left for an old colleague. How sad.
But you and I both know I have every right to be here — as an uninvited guest.
Stop it!
Why keep on fighting when you know it won't change anything? You know you won't win, not even now.
I know. And that's why I came with some help this time.
A cheap little trick. All that will do is buy you a little time...

dialogue.sit:
You simply do not understand, Aksinya. The sacrifice has already been made. That means the ending has already been set in motion, and there is nothing you can do to stop it.
So I failed this time. But what difference does it make? It's just one more "rehearsal"...
Next time... Next time, it will work...

"The clock strikes again."
A cold voice whispers the words in your ear. You know this isn't the first time you've heard something like this before.
In that voice, you hear a soul taking shape, polished by countless trials until it slowly grows to be more beautiful. That is, if pain, too, could be called beautiful...
In that same voice, you hear a soul taking form, growing ever more magnificent as it undergoes an endless process of transcendence. That is, if distortion, too, could be called magnificent...

Each time brings greater pain than the last.
Each time brings you closer to the thing you've been longing for...
And yet...
The mouth opens, then slowly closes again. It is too late. No words can stop what has already begun.
After all, that wish matters more than anything now.

"Yes. The clock strikes again. So let us begin once more. Your..."
You say you know you've heard these words before...
"Mine."
"'Ours...'"
"This endless 'wedding' of ours."

dialogue.t: Paimon's starting to feel a little nervous. It's like the Chicken-Mushroom Skewer she had this morning is dancing around in her stomach... Ugh.
Paimon wonders what Pavlina, the princess of the Snegurochka, is like... and what kind of person the groom is, too...
If Aglaya's story is anything to go by, Pavlina sounds completely enchanted with him. Humans even tried to steal him away! He must be some once-in-a-lifetime heartthrob.
...Maybe this wedding is more than it seems.
If what {NICKNAME} saw in the Pale Crown Palace really happened, then Pavlina was one of the people who betrayed Miss Aksinya... Which means...
Pavlina probably has one of the pieces of your body.
Right. The one who has the fragmented power of my body is... Ikhor. So I suspect the groom may be...
Pavlina! Pavlina!
Whoa! Where did she come from?
She's the mistress of this place. A trick like that is child's play for her.
But... no. How did she...?

dialogue.sit: What have you found out?

dialogue.t: Just as I expected. She carries a piece of my body's power in her life too.
Huh?

Love is what truly feeds the soul.
We were born without souls, so we chased after love because we longed to have one. We live for love, and we live because of love.
Yes. Human love is what gives us souls. It is what allows us to become beings in our own right.
But the humans who share their souls with us, they can be such terrible creditors who end up forcing us to live by the rules of their fickle love...
